concerns.text: Tasks T035–T042 (Review Resolution phases) implement architectural extensions (dual-timescale memory, uncertainty modules) that are not authorized by any Functional Requirement (FR) or User Story in spec.md. This constitutes unapproved scope creep and violates the constraint that tasks must not introduce features absent from the spec/plan.

Task T024 implements a 'TinyLSTM baseline' but fails to include the mandatory 'int8 weight quantization' required by spec.md US-2 Acceptance Scenario 3 and FR-004 to meet the 7GB RAM constraint. This is a semantic weakening of the baseline requirement.

Task T026 generates 'generated_stories.jsonl' but does not specify whether the output comes from the Brain-Inspired model or the Baseline model. Spec.md US-2 requires generating stories from *both* models to enable the comparison defined in FR-005. The task is underspecified and risks failing the comparison requirement.

Tasks T013 and T017 define output paths as `data/neural/processed/`, but the plan.md and spec.md define the processed data root as `data/processed/`. This path drift violates the 'Single Source of Truth' principle (Constitution Principle IV) and breaks traceability to the spec's data model.

Task T027 sets an internal memory target of '< 6GB', whereas spec.md SC-002 and FR-004 define the success criterion against the hardware limit of 7GB. Arbitrarily tightening the constraint in the task without spec authorization is a silent relaxation of the testable boundary condition.
